title: Lombardia Keeps Its Discount at the Pump, But the Methane Gap With Italy Is Closing Fast
dek: A near-flat day in Lombardia masks a four-month divergence: GPL and Metano have climbed faster here than nationally, even as the region holds cheaper prices across all four fuels.
executive_summary: On November 27, 2026, Lombardia's self-service drivers paid €1.9352/L for Benzina, €2.2203/L for Gasolio, €0.8181/L for GPL and €1.9711/L for Metano — all unchanged to only marginally lower than the day before. Against the national self-service averages of €1.9403, €2.22, €0.834 and €2.1131 respectively, Lombardia stays cheaper across the board, most dramatically for Metano, where the region's price sits 6.72% below the rest of Italy. Of the region's 3,088 registered stations, 2,830 (91.65%) reported prices today, a touch above the national reporting rate of 90.47%.

Zoom out to the 18 weeks of data tracked since July 21, though, and a sharper story emerges. Benzina and Gasolio have moved in near lockstep with the national market — down roughly 1.5% and up about 2.2% respectively since midsummer — but GPL and Metano have told very different stories. GPL in Lombardia has risen 14.66% since July, nearly five points faster than Italy's 9.81%, closing what was a 6% regional discount down to under 2% by late November. Metano has moved the same way but much faster in just the last three tracked weeks: Lombardia's price climbed 5.44% versus 1.98% nationally, trimming the region's discount from nearly 10% in early November to 6.85% today — the most interesting cross-fuel divergence in this report.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina: Lombardia Edges Below the National Average, Extending a Four-Month Slide
paragraphs: Lombardia's self-service Benzina price fell to €1.9352/L on November 27, down 0.24% from €1.9398/L the day before. That puts the region 0.26% below the national self-service average of €1.9403/L, a modest discount that has held for roughly two weeks.

Since tracking began on July 21 (a weekly average of €1.9722/L in week W30), Lombardia's Benzina price has fallen 1.50% to €1.9426/L by week W48, essentially tracking the 1.40% national decline over the same 18 weeks (€1.9756 to €1.9479). In between, prices in both series peaked in mid-to-late September — €2.1653/L in Lombardia and €2.1669/L nationally in week W39 — before retreating; Lombardia's pullback of 10.28% from that peak was slightly steeper than Italy's 10.11%, suggesting the region's pump prices reacted a touch more aggressively to the autumn correction than the rest of the country.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio: A Flat Day Caps a Season That Still Tracks Italy Almost Exactly
paragraphs: Gasolio eased slightly to €2.2203/L self-service in Lombardia on November 27, down 0.05% day over day, and now sits almost exactly level with the €2.22/L national average — a gap of just €0.0003/L, effectively a tie.

The bigger picture: Lombardia's Gasolio price has risen 2.23% since week W30 (€2.1744 to €2.2228 by W48), tracking the national increase of 2.22% (€2.1747 to €2.2229) almost to the decimal. Both series peaked in week W39 during the September run-up — €2.3784/L in Lombardia versus €2.3736/L nationally — before easing back by 6.54% and 6.35% respectively into late November, making Gasolio the fuel with the closest regional-to-national symmetry of the four tracked this period.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL: Lombardia's Discount Keeps Shrinking as Its Price Climbs Faster Than Italy's
paragraphs: GPL self-service held flat at €0.8181/L in Lombardia on November 27, unchanged from the previous day, and remains 1.91% cheaper than the €0.834/L national average.

That regional discount has been steadily eroding. Lombardia's GPL price has climbed 14.66% since week W30 (€0.7135 to €0.8181), nearly five percentage points faster than the national rise of 9.81% (€0.7592 to €0.8337) over the same 18 weeks. As a result, the gap between Lombardia and the rest of Italy has narrowed from roughly 6.02% in late July to just 1.87% by late November — among the fuels tracked, GPL's regional discount has closed the fastest over the full period.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano: Still Italy's Biggest Regional Discount, But the Gap Is Closing Fast
paragraphs: Metano self-service edged down to €1.9711/L in Lombardia on November 27, a marginal 0.10% dip from the day before, and remains by far the region's largest discount versus the rest of the country — 6.72% below the €2.1131/L national average.

That discount has been shrinking quickly in the most recent weeks of tracked data. Comparing week W45 (early November) to week W48 (late November), Lombardia's Metano price rose 5.44% (€1.8658 to €1.9672), nearly three times the national rise of 1.98% (€2.071 to €2.1119) over the same three weeks. That has narrowed the regional gap from 9.91% below the national price in early November to 6.85% by month's end — the fastest-closing price gap of any fuel tracked this period, and the most notable cross-fuel trend in this report.

network_section.heading: Station Network: A Slight Pullback, a Slightly Better Reporting Rate
paragraphs: Lombardia has 3,088 registered fuel stations as of November 27, down from 3,117 at the start of the tracked period in July — a net decline of 29 stations, or 0.93%, over 18 weeks. Of today's registered stations, 2,830 reported prices, for a 91.65% reporting rate.

That reporting rate sits comfortably above the national average of 90.47% (21,703 of 23,990 registered stations reporting today), suggesting Lombardia's network — despite shrinking modestly over the summer and autumn — keeps slightly better day-to-day price compliance than the rest of the country. The number of reporting stations fell from 2,869 in July to 2,830 today, a 1.36% decline that roughly tracks the overall drop in registrations, implying the stations that closed were not disproportionately drawn from either active reporters or dormant ones.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made: Zero Manual Spreadsheet Work
paragraphs: Everything in this report — the underlying price and station data pulled from MIMIT's daily feed, the rotating selection of today's featured region, the week-by-week trend analysis above, and the prose you're reading right now — is produced automatically every day by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. No analyst opens a spreadsheet, no one manually calculates week-over-week percentage changes, and no editor drafts the regional narrative; a scheduled agent runs the full chain end to end, from data ingestion through to this document and the accompanying social post.

That stands in contrast to how a project like this traditionally gets built: a manually-maintained Excel sheet, updated by hand each morning, with charts rebuilt and commentary rewritten by a person every single day. The Fuel Dashboard pipeline swaps that recurring manual labor for a one-time investment in automation — the data refresh, the regional rotation logic, the trend computation, and the report generation all run unattended, which is also why the region spotlighted here changes daily on a fixed, auditable rotation rather than editorial choice.

pull_quote: Lombardia's Metano discount to the rest of Italy has shrunk from nearly 10% to under 7% in just three weeks — the fastest-moving price gap of any fuel tracked this autumn.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Lombardia. The region holds a discount on every fuel versus the rest of Italy, but the most interesting number isn't today's price — it's how fast that gap is moving. Lombardia's Metano price has climbed 5.44% in just the last three tracked weeks, nearly three times the national rate, closing its discount from almost 10% to under 7% in that span. GPL shows the same pattern over the full four months tracked: Lombardia's price rose 14.66% since July versus 9.81% nationally, nearly erasing what was a 6% regional discount.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, self-updating site that tracks fuel prices across all 20 Italian regions, every province and municipality, and by individual operator/brand, refreshed daily from Italy's official MIMIT feed. Every piece of it, from the data pull to the regional rotation to the trend write-up behind today's report, runs automatically. No one opens Excel each morning to update a chart.

That's the real point: this dashboard and its ~10-page regional report were built with Claude Code instead of a manually-maintained spreadsheet. A tool like this used to mean someone's recurring daily chore. Now it's a pipeline that runs itself, which is exactly the kind of thing AI coding tools are good for: turning a daily manual task into a one-time build.
